Every rule the agent can record (93): the production engine's rules and the 8 the agent issues outside the engine (NN-L-AT-001_AntiTamperDenial, NN-L-EPG-001_CredentialPostcondition, NN-L-EPG-002_NamespaceRootPostcondition, NN-L-EXECQ-001_FirstSightQuarantine, NN-L-EXECPOL-001_StagingExecDenied, NN-L-EXECENV-001_PreloadFromStaging, NN-L-EXECENV-002_ExecEnvironmentTrick, NN-L-EXECENV-003_ExecMappingFromStaging). For each: its severities and responses (the strongest first), its ATT&CK references ([`ATTACK_COVERAGE.md`](ATTACK_COVERAGE.md)), the sensor and data it reads, its validation status — for a rule in the V2 Critical sub-gate the status [`matrix.md`](../validation/matrix.md) gives it, for any other the kinds of test its entry cites ([`v2-rules.tsv`](../validation/v2-rules.tsv); `lab` names a lab script that exercises the rule, not a recorded lab run) —, what it observes, its known false positives and how to make it fire.

MITRE ATT&CK® Enterprise 20.0: the ids, tactics and names are MITRE's, from the pinned list [`attack-enterprise-20.0.tsv`](attack-enterprise-20.0.tsv) (bundle `enterprise-attack/enterprise-attack-20.0.json` of https://github.com/mitre-attack/attack-stix-data at commit `20664a889568dce884a1dac0ec7b12ae3a199f51`, sha256 `81113ba98afa2928f3dcff62022539f7ce30c315c32e14422f11ff95ce534352`), under the ATT&CK Terms of Use ([`LICENSES/MITRE_ATTACK_ToU-20.0.md`](../../LICENSES/MITRE_ATTACK_ToU-20.0.md), `NOTICES.md`).

### R001_ExecFromTmp

Exec from /tmp/ — category `execution`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | Medium |
| Response | KillProcessTree |
| ATT&CK | T1059 Command and Scripting Interpreter (Execution) |
| Sensor — data | exec (sched_process_exec, bprm_check_security) — DC0032 Process Creation |
| Validation | unit+e2e+lab |

**Observes.** The exec of a file under `/tmp/`, judged on the file the kernel executed (a relative path, a symlink or `..` resolves to it).

**Known false positives.** An installer or a build that runs what it unpacked in `/tmp` is killed: the rule's whitelist is empty and the process allowlist does not apply. A root exec in an administrator's sudo/su session or a package transaction is R009's Low record instead (R009 runs first).

**How to test.** As an unprivileged user: `cp /bin/true /tmp/nn-r001 && /tmp/nn-r001`. Run as root it is R009's verdict.

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/r001_exec_from_tmp.rs::fires_on_exec_from_tmp`, `agent/tests/response_privileged_e2e.rs::tmp_dropper_forked_child_dies_with_it`, `deploy/lab/exec-sensor/exec-sensor-check.sh::R001_ExecFromTmp`

**ATT&CK note.** No technique is "execution from a staging directory": T1059 follows design §7.1 and V2 row TQ18 (the script or shell a dropper runs). A native payload is evidence of the Execution tactic, not of an interpreter.

### R002_ExecFromDevShm

Exec from /dev/shm/ — category `execution`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | High |
| Response | KillProcessTree |
| ATT&CK | T1059 Command and Scripting Interpreter (Execution); T1027.011 Obfuscated Files or Information: Fileless Storage (Stealth) |
| Sensor — data | exec (sched_process_exec, bprm_check_security) — DC0032 Process Creation |
| Validation | unit |

**Observes.** The exec of a file under `/dev/shm/`, the memory-backed shared directory, judged on the file the kernel executed.

**Known false positives.** Rare: few programs execute from `/dev/shm`. Nothing exempts one that does.

**How to test.** As an unprivileged user: `cp /bin/true /dev/shm/nn-r002 && /dev/shm/nn-r002` (a host that mounts `/dev/shm` noexec refuses the exec before the rule sees it).

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/r002_exec_from_dev_shm.rs::fires_on_dev_shm`, `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/r002_exec_from_dev_shm.rs::r002_kills_the_process_tree`

**ATT&CK note.** T1027.011 names `/dev/shm` as fileless storage; T1059 as for R001.

### R004_ExecFromProcSelfFd

Exec from /proc/<pid>/fd/* (memfd) — category `execution`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | Critical |
| Response | KillProcessTree |
| ATT&CK | T1620 Reflective Code Loading (Stealth) |
| Sensor — data | exec (sched_process_exec, bprm_check_security) — DC0032 Process Creation |
| Validation | e2e (V2 Critical sub-gate) |

**Observes.** A fileless exec: with the exec sensor's identity, a memfd, or an unlinked file reached through a descriptor; without it (tracepoint mode), an exec path of the form `/proc/self/fd/N`, `/proc/<pid>/fd/N`, `/dev/fd/N` or `/memfd:`.

**Known false positives.** systemd-executor's launch of every unit (systemd 254 and later) is exempt on what the kernel executed and on a systemd parent. Another program that re-executes itself from a memfd (older runc versions do, to protect their binary) is killed: nothing else is exempt.

**How to test.** `python3 -c 'import os; fd = os.memfd_create("x"); os.write(fd, open("/bin/true", "rb").read()); os.execv("/proc/self/fd/%d" % fd, ["x"])'`.

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/r004_exec_from_proc_self_fd.rs::fires_on_proc_self_fd`, `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/r004_exec_from_proc_self_fd.rs::fires_on_a_memfd_whatever_path_reached_it`, `agent/tests/detection_rules_at_scale_privileged_e2e.rs::process_memfd_fileless_exec_trips_r004`, `deploy/lab/exec-sensor/exec-sensor-check.sh::R004_ExecFromProcSelfFd`

**ATT&CK note.** T1620: an anonymous (memfd) or unlinked file executed through a descriptor is a payload with no file on disk.

### R005_NetcatExec

Netcat family launched — category `lateral_movement`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | High |
| Response | Log |
| ATT&CK | T1095 Non-Application Layer Protocol (Command and Control) |
| Sensor — data | exec (sched_process_exec, bprm_check_security) — DC0032 Process Creation |
| Validation | unit |

**Observes.** An exec whose `comm` is a netcat (`nc`, `ncat`, `netcat`, `nc.openbsd`, `nc.traditional`), recorded only.

**Known false positives.** Administrators and scripts use netcat for port checks and file transfers; every such exec is recorded (Log), none is acted on. The name is the process's own: a renamed copy is not seen.

**How to test.** `nc -z 127.0.0.1 22` (any netcat invocation).

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/r005_netcat_exec.rs::fires_on_each_netcat_alias`

**ATT&CK note.** T1095 for netcat's use as a raw TCP/UDP channel (a reverse or bind shell); the rule sees the name only, not the connection.

### R006_ReverseShellTooling

Reverse shell tooling — category `lateral_movement`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | Critical, High |
| Response | KillProcessTree, Log |
| ATT&CK | T1095 Non-Application Layer Protocol (Command and Control); T1059.004 Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell (Execution) |
| Sensor — data | exec (sched_process_exec, bprm_check_security) — DC0032 Process Creation |
| Validation | unit (V2 Critical sub-gate) |

**Observes.** An exec named like offensive tooling (`socat`, `msfvenom`, `meterpreter`, `sliver`, `havoc`). The distribution's `socat` is recorded unless one of its addresses runs a shell (`EXEC:`, `SYSTEM:`, `SHELL:`), and recorded at Critical when the kernel cut its argv.

**Known false positives.** A `socat` from `/usr/bin`, `/bin`, `/usr/sbin` or `/sbin` used as a relay is recorded (Log, High), not killed; a build of it elsewhere is killed unless allowlisted in `process-comm-allowlist`, which is judged on what the kernel executed.

**How to test.** `cp /bin/sleep /tmp/sliver && /tmp/sliver 5` (killed); `socat -V` (the distribution's socat, recorded).

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/r006_reverse_shell_tooling.rs::fires_on_each_offsec_tool`, `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/r006_reverse_shell_tooling.rs::r006_system_socat_is_recorded_a_copy_is_killed`, `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/r006_reverse_shell_tooling.rs::r006_system_socat_running_a_shell_is_killed`

**ATT&CK note.** The tools are C2 frameworks and a relay: T1095 for the raw TCP channel, T1059.004 for the shell `socat EXEC:` runs. The rule sees the name and argv, not the traffic; a renamed tool evades it.

### R007_CryptoMiner

Crypto miner — category `resource_abuse`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | Critical, High |
| Response | KillProcessTree, Log |
| ATT&CK | T1496.001 Resource Hijacking: Compute Hijacking (Impact) |
| Sensor — data | exec (sched_process_exec, bprm_check_security) — DC0032 Process Creation |
| Validation | unit (V2 Critical sub-gate) |

**Observes.** An exec whose `comm`, or the basename of the file the kernel executed, is a miner's name (`xmrig`, `cpuminer`, `minerd`, `ccminer`, `ethminer`, `phoenixminer`), any case: killed. A name that only contains one is recorded, from a second registration after every process rule that kills.

**Known false positives.** A cleanup or monitoring tool named after a miner (`xmrig-cleanup`) is recorded, not killed; a benchmark run of a real miner is killed unless allowlisted in `process-comm-allowlist`.

**How to test.** `cp /bin/sleep ~/xmrig && ~/xmrig 5` (killed); `cp /bin/sleep ~/xmrig-check && ~/xmrig-check 5` (recorded).

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/r007_crypto_miner.rs::fires_on_known_miner_comms`, `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/r007_crypto_miner.rs::r007_substring_only_is_recorded`

**ATT&CK note.** T1496.001 Compute Hijacking, v20's sub-technique for mining. By name only: the CPU and pool connections of a renamed miner are not judged here.

### R008_HiddenHomeBinary

Executable in hidden user directory — category `persistence`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | Medium |
| Response | Log |
| ATT&CK | T1564.001 Hide Artifacts: Hidden Files and Directories (Stealth) |
| Sensor — data | exec (sched_process_exec, bprm_check_security) — DC0032 Process Creation |
| Validation | unit |

**Observes.** The exec of a native file under a dot-directory of a home (`/home/<user>/.<dir>/`), outside the toolchain directories the rule lists; recorded only.

**Known false positives.** Toolchains and tools that run their own downloads are exempt by directory (`.cargo/bin`, `.local/bin`, `.rustup`, `.nvm`, the named caches under `.cache` and `.config`); another one is recorded.

**How to test.** `mkdir -p ~/.nn-r008 && cp /bin/true ~/.nn-r008/x && ~/.nn-r008/x`.

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/r008_hidden_home_binary.rs::fires_on_unknown_dot_directory`, `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/r008_hidden_home_binary.rs::autostart_dir_is_never_exempt`

**ATT&CK note.** T1564.001: only the hiding is observed, not the persistence a hidden binary may serve.

### R009_RootExecFromUserPath

Root exec from user-writable path — category `privilege_escalation`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | High, Low |
| Response | KillProcessTree, Log |
| ATT&CK | T1548 Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism (Privilege Escalation); T1068 Exploitation for Privilege Escalation (Privilege Escalation) |
| Sensor — data | exec (sched_process_exec, bprm_check_security) — DC0032 Process Creation |
| Validation | unit+e2e |

**Observes.** An exec by uid 0 of a file under `/home/`, `/tmp/` or `/var/tmp/`, judged on the file the kernel executed.

**Known false positives.** An administrator's sudo/su session at a terminal and a package transaction (a package manager run by root whose run covers the exec) are recorded at Low, not killed. Root automation outside both (a root cron job or a configuration-management run that executes a file from a home or `/tmp`) is killed.

**How to test.** `cp /bin/true /tmp/nn-r009 && sudo systemd-run --wait /tmp/nn-r009` (root, outside a terminal session).

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/r009_root_exec_from_user_path.rs::fires_on_root_in_user_path`, `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/r009_root_exec_from_user_path.rs::sudo_session_at_a_terminal_is_recorded_not_killed`, `agent/tests/response_privileged_e2e.rs::tmp_dropper_forked_child_dies_with_it`

**ATT&CK note.** The rule sees the result, root executing a file a user can write, not the means: T1548 (an abused setuid binary or sudo rule) and T1068 (an exploit) are the escalations it is evidence of.

### R010_BinaryInWebroot

Exec from web document root — category `execution`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | High |
| Response | KillProcessTree |
| ATT&CK | T1505.003 Server Software Component: Web Shell (Persistence) |
| Sensor — data | exec (sched_process_exec, bprm_check_security) — DC0032 Process Creation |
| Validation | unit |

**Observes.** The exec of a file under a web server's document root (`/var/www/`, `/srv/www/`, `/usr/share/nginx/html/`, `/var/lib/nginx/`, `/var/lib/apache2/`), judged on the file the kernel executed.

**Known false positives.** A CGI program installed under one of these roots is killed; nothing exempts it. Interpreted pages (PHP) run their interpreter from `/usr/bin` and do not match.

### R011_KernelModuleTooling

Kernel-module tooling exec — category `persistence`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | High |
| Response | KillProcessTree, KillProcess, Log |
| ATT&CK | T1547.006 Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Kernel Modules and Extensions (Persistence) |
| Sensor — data | exec (sched_process_exec, bprm_check_security) — DC0032 Process Creation |
| Validation | unit+e2e+lab |

**Observes.** The exec of `insmod`, `modprobe` or `kmod` whose parent is not a kernel thread (`PF_KTHREAD`, read by the sensor). A copy run from a staging directory is killed with its tree, the tool elsewhere alone.

**Known false positives.** Kernel-driven loads (a kworker's modprobe at boot or hot-plug) are exempt. A root exec of the system's tool under a trusted actor of `process-comm-allowlist` (DKMS under apt or dpkg) is recorded, not killed; an administrator's manual `modprobe` is killed unless the tool itself is allowlisted.

**How to test.** `sudo modprobe dummy` (anti-tamper.sh case C16).

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/r011_kernel_module_tooling.rs::fires_on_kmod_tooling`, `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/r011_kernel_module_tooling.rs::kmod_tool_under_apt_is_recorded_not_killed`, `agent/tests/detection_rules_at_scale_privileged_e2e.rs::process_kernel_module_tooling_trips_r011`, `deploy/lab/adversarial/anti-tamper.sh::case C16`

**ATT&CK note.** The tool's exec, not the load itself (R018).

### R012_SetcapTooling

Capability-set tooling exec — category `privilege_escalation`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | High |
| Response | KillProcessTree, KillProcess, Log |
| ATT&CK | T1548 Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism (Privilege Escalation) |
| Sensor — data | exec (sched_process_exec, bprm_check_security) — DC0032 Process Creation |
| Validation | unit |

**Observes.** The exec of `setcap`, which grants file capabilities; a capability spec in argv is named in the reasoning. A copy run from a staging directory is killed with its tree.

**Known false positives.** A provisioning tool that sets capabilities is killed unless `setcap` is allowlisted in `process-comm-allowlist`; under a trusted actor (a package manager) the system's `setcap` is recorded. A capability set by any other route is NN-L-FIM-025's.

**How to test.** `setcap` with no argument (the exec alone fires it).

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/r012_setcap_tooling.rs::fires_on_setcap`, `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/r012_setcap_tooling.rs::r012_staged_copy_kills_the_process_tree`

**ATT&CK note.** File capabilities have no sub-technique of their own (T1548.001 is setuid and setgid): the parent technique.

### R013_NamespaceEscapeTooling

Namespace/escape tooling from non-standard path — category `privilege_escalation`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | High |
| Response | KillProcessTree, KillProcess, Log |
| ATT&CK | T1611 Escape to Host (Privilege Escalation) |
| Sensor — data | exec (sched_process_exec, bprm_check_security) — DC0032 Process Creation |
| Validation | unit |

**Observes.** The exec of `nsenter`, `unshare` or `runc` from outside `/usr/bin`, `/bin`, `/usr/sbin` and `/sbin`; host-escape flags in argv (`-t`, `--mount`, `--privileged`, `--net=host`) are named in the reasoning.

**Known false positives.** A container runtime that runs its own `runc` from a non-standard path (a bundled runtime under `/var/lib` or `/opt`) is killed until `runc` is allowlisted in `process-comm-allowlist` (`docs/operator/CONTAINER_HOST_DEPLOY.md`). An empty exec path never fires.

**How to test.** `cp /usr/bin/unshare ~/unshare && ~/unshare --help`.

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/r013_namespace_escape_tooling.rs::fires_on_escape_tool_from_nonstandard_path`, `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/r013_namespace_escape_tooling.rs::r013_staged_copy_kills_the_process_tree`

**ATT&CK note.** The tool's exec from an odd place is the escape attempt's shape; the escape itself (a write to the host's namespaces) is not observed.

### R014_AtBatchScheduling

at/batch scheduling exec — category `persistence`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | Medium |
| Response | Log |
| ATT&CK | T1053.002 Scheduled Task/Job: At (Persistence); T1053.002 Scheduled Task/Job: At (Execution) |
| Sensor — data | exec (sched_process_exec, bprm_check_security) — DC0032 Process Creation |
| Validation | unit |

**Observes.** The exec of `at` or `batch`, with the time spec from argv; recorded only.

**Known false positives.** Administrators schedule one-shot jobs routinely; every one is recorded, none acted on. `process-comm-allowlist` silences it.

**How to test.** `echo true | at now + 1 minute` (the `at` package installed).

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/r014_at_batch_scheduling.rs::fires_on_scheduling_tool`

**ATT&CK note.** Execution and Persistence, the two tactics of T1053.002 a one-shot job serves; the job's own run later is an ordinary exec.

### R015_EncodingToolingServiceUid

Encoding tooling exec by service account — category `defense_evasion`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | Medium |
| Response | Log |
| ATT&CK | T1027 Obfuscated Files or Information (Stealth); T1140 Deobfuscate/Decode Files or Information (Stealth); T1132 Data Encoding (Command and Control) |
| Sensor — data | exec (sched_process_exec, bprm_check_security) — DC0032 Process Creation |
| Validation | unit |

**Observes.** The exec of `base64`, `xxd` or `openssl` by a service account (uid 1..999, `nobody`, systemd's `DynamicUser=` range); decode or cipher flags in argv are named. Recorded only.

**Known false positives.** A daemon that legitimately shells out to `openssl` (a certificate renewal under a service account, a backup script) is recorded; `process-comm-allowlist` silences it. Root and human users are out of scope.

**How to test.** `sudo -u nobody base64 /etc/hostname`.

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/r015_encoding_tooling_service_uid.rs::fires_on_encoder_by_service_uid`, `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/r015_encoding_tooling_service_uid.rs::nobody_is_service_class`

**ATT&CK note.** T1027 for an encode, T1140 for a decode (`base64 -d`), T1132 as V2 row TQ29: the rule sees the encoder's exec, not the data or the channel.

| Validation | unit |

**Observes.** The exec of `gdb`, `strace` or `ltrace` by a service account (the class of R015); an attach to a live process (`-p`, `--pid`) is named. Recorded only.

**Known false positives.** A crash handler or a CI runner under a system account that runs a debugger is recorded; `process-comm-allowlist` silences it. Root and human users are out of scope.

**How to test.** `sudo -u nobody gdb --version` (gdb installed).

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/r016_debugger_service_uid.rs::fires_on_debugger_by_service_uid`, `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/r016_debugger_service_uid.rs::argv_attach_pid_enriches_reasoning`

**ATT&CK note.** The rule's prose named T1622 (Debugger Evasion) until lab PR 221: a payload detecting a debugger, not running one. What it observes is a ptrace tracer started by a service account, the tool of T1055.008; a service account traces only its own processes, so Stealth, not Privilege Escalation. The ptrace call itself is not seen (V2 row TQ14 stays a known gap).

### R017_ShellFromNonstandardPath

Shell binary from non-standard path — category `execution`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | High |
| Response | KillProcessTree, Log |
| ATT&CK | T1059.004 Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell (Execution) |
| Sensor — data | exec (sched_process_exec, bprm_check_security) — DC0032 Process Creation |
| Validation | unit+e2e |

**Observes.** The exec of a shell (`comm` `sh`, `bash` or `dash`) from outside the root-only shell directories (`/bin`, `/usr/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `/usr/sbin`, `/sbin`, `/nix/store`); an inline `-c` payload and the parent are named.

**Known false positives.** A shell bundled under `/opt` or in a home (a vendored busybox, a conda environment) is killed unless allowlisted in `process-comm-allowlist`; under a trusted actor the record replaces the kill. An empty exec path never fires.

**How to test.** `cp /bin/sh ~/sh && ~/sh -c true`.

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/r017_shell_from_nonstandard_path.rs::fires_on_shell_from_nonstandard_path`, `agent/tests/detection_rules_at_scale_privileged_e2e.rs::process_shell_from_nonstandard_path_trips_r017`

### R018_KernelModuleLoad

Kernel module load — category `rootkit`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | Critical, High, Medium |
| Response | KillProcessTree, Log |
| ATT&CK | T1547.006 Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Kernel Modules and Extensions (Persistence); T1014 Rootkit (Stealth) |
| Sensor — data | kernel module load (kernel_read_file, kernel_load_data) — DC0031 Kernel Module Load |
| Validation | unit (V2 Critical sub-gate) |

**Observes.** A kernel module load (`finit_module`, `init_module`) at the LSM hooks. Killed: a file outside `/lib/modules`, a path deeper than any module directory, or a file under it that no package installed and DKMS did not build, loaded by an unexpected loader. Recorded: a legacy `init_module` (High), an unreadable path (High), a standard module by an unexpected loader (Medium).

**Known false positives.** Kernel-driven loads are exempt, and so are `systemd-udevd`, `systemd-modules-load` and `kmod` (loader or parent) for a module in a module directory. An administrator who loads a module from a build directory (`insmod ~/driver.ko`) is killed.

**How to test.** Copy an in-tree module out of the module tree, decompressed, and `insmod` it from `/tmp` (Critical); `exec -a modprobe` of a renamed loader for a standard module (anti-tamper.sh case C58, Medium).

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/r018_kernel_module_load.rs::fire_nonstandard_path_is_critical_killtree`, `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/r018_kernel_module_load.rs::fire_stdpath_unexpected_loader_is_medium_log`, `deploy/lab/adversarial/anti-tamper.sh::case C58`

### R020_ShellWithSocketStdio

Shell or interpreter with stdin/stdout on a network socket — category `execution`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | Critical |
| Response | Log |
| ATT&CK | T1059.004 Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell (Execution); T1095 Non-Application Layer Protocol (Command and Control) |
| Sensor — data | exec (sched_process_exec, bprm_check_security) — DC0032 Process Creation, DC0082 Network Connection Creation |
| Validation | unit (V2 Critical sub-gate) |

**Observes.** A shell or interpreter, by exec identity, whose stdin/stdout is an outbound inet socket (the reverse shell), or an accepted one not handed over by an inetd-style launcher (the bind shell), or whose parent's stdio is an outbound socket (the pty-wrapped reverse shell): `sched_process_exec` reads the new image's fds 0..2 and its parent's. Critical, recorded, posture ConfirmedIntrusion; the kill of the tree (`KillProcessTree`) is held behind the per-rule response policy, off by default (a new rule of lab PR 224).

**Known false positives.** inetd-style services (PID 1 socket activation, inetd, xinetd, tcpserver), exempt by the launcher's identity; the process allowlist by identity. Without the optional BTF offsets the stdio is not read and the rule cannot fire.

**How to test.** `net-check.sh --only MS06`: bash on a /dev/tcp socket, and the Python pty reverse shell (MS06B), to a loopback listener.

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/r020_shell_with_socket_stdio.rs::a_shell_on_an_outbound_socket_is_a_critical_reverse_shell`, `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/r020_shell_with_socket_stdio.rs::a_pty_wrapped_reverse_shell_fires_on_the_shell`, `deploy/lab/malsim/net-check.sh::MS06`

**ATT&CK note.** The shell (T1059.004) and its raw channel (T1095), as R006 maps the tools that set one up.

### NN-L-EXECQ-001_FirstSightQuarantine

Exec quarantine at first sight — category `malware_prevention`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | Critical, High, Medium, Low |
| Response | Quarantine, KillProcess, Log |
| ATT&CK | T1204.002 User Execution: Malicious File (Execution); T1059.004 Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell (Execution); T1059.006 Command and Scripting Interpreter: Python (Execution); T1059.007 Command and Scripting Interpreter: JavaScript (Execution); T1059 Command and Scripting Interpreter (Execution) |
| Sensor — data | exec (sched_process_exec, bprm_check_security) — DC0032 Process Creation, DC0059 File Metadata |
| Validation | no proof |

**Observes.** With --exec-quarantine: an executable never judged before, run from a guarded location (/tmp, /var/tmp, /dev/shm, a home or world-writable directory, a memfd, an unlinked file), held by the kernel before its first instruction (enforce) and judged by the confined scanner (signed hash list, ELF and script heuristics) and the rules; resumed, or killed and quarantined. Recorded by the guard's controller, one record per decision.

**Known false positives.** A build or a test suite running new binaries from a home or /tmp: judged once per identity, resumed when clean (cached), and the default policy resumes on an expired budget; a suspicious verdict resumes unless --exec-quarantine-on-suspicious kill.

**How to test.** On a lab guest, `nn-lab.sh execq-check`: copies of /usr/bin/true and /usr/bin/ls are resumed and cached, the block-listed marker binary is killed before it writes its marker and quarantined.

**Tests.** `agent/src/execq/controller/tests.rs::a_blocklisted_binary_is_killed_and_quarantined`, `agent/src/execq/controller/tests.rs::a_clean_new_binary_is_resumed_cached_and_recorded_once`, `deploy/lab/execq/execq-check.sh::execq check: PASS`

**ATT&CK note.** User Execution: Malicious File (T1204.002) for what it holds; a script also names its interpreter's technique (T1059.004, .006, .007, or T1059), per record.

### NN-L-FIM-001_SystemBinaryModified

System binary modified — category `fim_persistence`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | Critical, Low |
| Response | KillProcessTree, Log |
| ATT&CK | T1554 Compromise Host Software Binary (Persistence); T1548.001 Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Setuid and Setgid (Privilege Escalation) |
| Sensor — data | file (file_open LSM, FIM drift) — DC0061 File Modification, DC0059 File Metadata |
| Validation | unit (V2 Critical sub-gate) |

**Observes.** A rewrite of a watched file under /bin, /sbin, /usr/bin, /usr/sbin or /usr/lib, or a permission or ownership change there that hands out power over it (a set-id bit, write for group or others, a new owner).

**Known false positives.** Package upgrades rewrite these files: a write inside a package transaction (dpkg, rpm or dnf lineage, kernel-resolved) is recorded at Low. A change that only takes power away (chmod u-s) draws no verdict. A hand-built `make install` into /usr is killed.

**How to test.** `sudo chmod g+w /usr/bin/curl` (a watched binary), then `sudo chmod g-w /usr/bin/curl`; expect Critical, KillProcessTree aimed at chmod.

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/fim/rules.rs::fim001_fires_on_system_binary_modified`, `crates/nn-core/src/fim/rules.rs::a_set_uid_bit_on_a_system_binary_is_killed_its_removal_is_not`, `crates/nn-core/src/fim/rules.rs::package_manager_writes_are_logged_not_killed`

**ATT&CK note.** T1554 for a rewritten binary, T1548.001 for a set-id bit granted on one. A supply-chain compromise (T1195) happens upstream; the host sees the file change.

### NN-L-FIM-002_NewSuidBinary

New SUID-root binary appeared in user-writable dir — category `fim_evasion`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | Critical, Medium, Low |
| Response | KillProcessTree, Log |
| ATT&CK | T1548.001 Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Setuid and Setgid (Privilege Escalation) |
| Sensor — data | file (file_open LSM, FIM drift) — DC0039 File Creation |
| Validation | unit (V2 Critical sub-gate) |

**Observes.** A hard link, in /tmp, /var/tmp, /dev/shm or /home, to a watched inode (the kernel reports a link only when its source is watched, such as a setuid-root system binary): Critical. A file created in a watched directory there is recorded (Medium, Log): the hook carries no mode bits.

**Known false positives.** Files that browsers, GnuPG or SDKs create in watched home paths are only recorded (external audit FIMR-006). A link made inside a package transaction is recorded at Low.

**How to test.** `sudo ln /usr/bin/passwd /var/tmp/nn-link` (on the filesystem of /usr), then `sudo rm /var/tmp/nn-link`; expect Critical, KillProcessTree aimed at ln.

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/fim/rules.rs::fim002_kills_a_watched_inode_linked_into_a_user_writable_dir`, `crates/nn-core/src/fim/rules.rs::fim002_records_a_file_created_in_a_watched_user_writable_dir`

**ATT&CK note.** T1548.001: a setuid binary kept under a name a user controls. The rule does not see a set-id bit itself; NN-L-FIM-001 and NN-L-FIM-025 do.

### NN-L-FIM-003_SensitiveConfigModified

Sensitive config modified — category `fim_credential_access`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | High, Low |
| Response | KillProcess, Log |
| ATT&CK | T1098 Account Manipulation (Persistence); T1136.001 Create Account: Local Account (Persistence); T1556.003 Modify Authentication Process: Pluggable Authentication Modules (Persistence); T1548.003 Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Sudo and Sudo Caching (Privilege Escalation) |
| Sensor — data | file (file_open LSM, FIM drift) — DC0061 File Modification, DC0059 File Metadata |
| Validation | unit |

**Observes.** A rewrite of /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, /etc/sudoers, /etc/ssh/sshd_config, /etc/pam.d/sshd or /etc/pam.d/sudo, or a permission or ownership change of one that grants power or exposes its content (chmod o+r /etc/shadow).

**Known false positives.** Account administration writes these files. An account tool (passwd, useradd, chpasswd, systemd-sysusers and the rest, by kernel-resolved exe) is recorded, at Low when a non-root user ran it; a write in an administrator's interactive sudo or su session is recorded at High; a package transaction at Low. A configuration-management run without a terminal is killed.

**How to test.** `sudo systemd-run --wait chmod o+r /etc/shadow`, then `sudo chmod o-r /etc/shadow` (systemd-run: no terminal, so the interactive-admin carve-out does not apply); expect High, KillProcess.

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/fim/rules.rs::fim003_fires_on_sensitive_config_modified`, `crates/nn-core/src/fim/rules.rs::shadow_made_readable_by_others_is_a_sensitive_change`, `crates/nn-core/src/fim/rules.rs::account_tools_are_recorded_not_killed`

**ATT&CK note.** One technique per file: passwd and shadow are T1098 (an account changed) and T1136.001 (a local account added), the two PAM files T1556.003, sudoers T1548.003; sshd_config has none of its own. A read of shadow (T1003.008) is not this rule's: it fires on a write or a permission change.

### NN-L-FIM-004_AuthorizedKeysModified

SSH authorized_keys modified — category `fim_persistence`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | High |
| Response | KillProcess |
| ATT&CK | T1098.004 Account Manipulation: SSH Authorized Keys (Persistence) |
| Sensor — data | file (file_open LSM, FIM drift) — DC0061 File Modification, DC0039 File Creation, DC0059 File Metadata |
| Validation | unit |

**Observes.** A new or edited file sshd reads public keys from (~/.ssh/authorized_keys, ~/.ssh/authorized_keys2, /etc/ssh/authorized_keys, /etc/ssh/authorized_keys/&lt;user&gt;), or one handed to another owner or made writable by group or others.

**Known false positives.** No carve-out: an administrator adding a key by hand or with ssh-copy-id is killed after the write (the key stays). fim-paths.v1 watches root's files and /etc/ssh's; a user's home needs an entry in fim-paths.local.

**How to test.** `echo ssh-ed25519 AAAA nn-test | sudo tee -a /root/.ssh/authorized_keys` (the file must exist when the agent starts); expect High, KillProcess aimed at tee. Remove the line afterwards.

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/fim/rules.rs::fim004_fires_on_authorized_keys_modified`, `crates/nn-core/src/fim/rules.rs::fim004_fires_on_authorized_keys2_and_etc_ssh_forms`, `crates/nn-core/src/fim/rules.rs::an_authorized_keys_file_handed_to_another_owner_fires`

**ATT&CK note.** A new authorized_keys file created in a watched directory under /home is recorded by NN-L-FIM-002 (Medium, Log), which the engine evaluates first; an edit of an existing one, and any write under /root or /etc/ssh, is this rule's.

### NN-L-FIM-005_LogTruncated

Log file modified (truncation suspect) — category `fim_defense_evasion`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | High |
| Response | Log |
| ATT&CK | T1685.006 Disable or Modify Tools: Clear Linux or Mac System Logs (Defense Impairment) |
| Sensor — data | file (file_open LSM, FIM drift) — DC0061 File Modification |
| Validation | unit |

**Observes.** A rewrite of a watched file under /var/log or /var/audit (fim-paths.v1: auth.log, secure, syslog, messages, kern.log, audit/audit.log); the drift record says whether it shrank. wtmp, btmp and lastlog are left to NN-L-FIM-018 and -019.

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/fim/rules.rs::fim005_fires_on_log_modification_but_logs_only`, `crates/nn-core/src/fim/rules.rs::fim005_rsyslogd_truncation_still_fires`, `crates/nn-core/src/fim/rules.rs::fim005_non_rsyslogd_writer_still_fires`

### NN-L-FIM-006_OperatorBinaryModified

Operator-installed binary modified — category `fim_supply_chain`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | Medium |
| Response | Log |
| ATT&CK | T1554 Compromise Host Software Binary (Persistence) |
| Sensor — data | file (file_open LSM, FIM drift) — DC0061 File Modification |

### NN-L-FIM-007_CronDropInCreated

**ATT&CK note.** T1685 (Disable or Modify Tools), which replaced T1562.001 in ATT&CK v19; the reasoning text, pinned by a test, still names T1562.001.

### NN-L-FIM-025_FileCapabilityGranted

File capability granted — category `fim_privilege_escalation`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | Critical, High, Medium, Low |
| Response | StripFileCapability, Log |
| ATT&CK | T1548 Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism (Privilege Escalation) |
| Sensor — data | file (file_open LSM, FIM drift) — DC0059 File Metadata |
| Validation | unit (V2 Critical sub-gate) |

**Observes.** A file capability (security.capability) stored on any file, by any route (setcap, setxattr, cp --preserve=xattr, tar --xattrs), seen by the file-open sensor's inode_post_setxattr hook. Critical for a root-equivalent capability (setuid, setgid, dac_override, dac_read_search, fowner, chown, sys_admin, sys_ptrace, sys_module, sys_rawio, setfcap, bpf), else High; the response removes it.

**Known false positives.** Packages install files with capabilities (ping, newuidmap, dumpcap): recorded at Low and kept. A grant in an interactive sudo or su session, or while the trusted-installer window is open, is recorded and kept; a namespaced capability (a rootless container build) is recorded at Medium.

**How to test.** `cp /usr/bin/python3 /tmp/nn-py && sudo systemd-run --wait setcap cap_setuid+ep /tmp/nn-py`; `getcap /tmp/nn-py` then prints nothing; expect Critical, StripFileCapability.

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/fim/rules.rs::fim025_strips_a_granted_capability`, `crates/nn-core/src/fim/rules.rs::fim025_keeps_a_grant_inside_the_trusted_installer_window`, `crates/nn-core/src/fim/rules.rs::fim025_package_manager_and_interactive_admin_keep_the_capability`

**ATT&CK note.** T1548: ATT&CK has no sub-technique for Linux file capabilities (T1548.001 is the set-id bits).

### NN-L-IMP-001_RansomwareEncryption

Ransomware encryption: two shapes of one process tree — category `impact_ransomware`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | Critical |
| Response | Log |
| ATT&CK | T1486 Data Encrypted for Impact (Impact) |
| Sensor — data | file (file_open LSM, FIM drift) — DC0061 File Modification, DC0039 File Creation, DC0040 File Deletion |
| Validation | unit (V2 Critical sub-gate) |

**Observes.** Two of four shapes of one actor's file activity within 120 s: existing files rewritten (the mass-write overwrite counter), ciphertext-like content left behind (entropy sampled in userland), a burst of renames to one new extension (or encrypted copies under an extension appended to the names of the originals deleted, the copies themselves sampled), deletion of originals after new files were written. Critical, recorded; the kill of the actor's tree (`KillProcessTree`) and the posture's COMBAT without corroboration are held behind the per-rule response policy, off by default (new in lab PR 225): the posture's RansomwareEncryption needs corroboration, ENGAGED alone, never locked.

**Known false positives.** Writers trusted by exec identity, package ownership and lineage, never by name: a root package transaction, or a packaged program with no foreign program in its lineage (rsync, tar, git, compilers, backup agents, databases), never counts. Copy-then-delete by anyone else — `mv` across filesystems, `rsync --remove-source-files`, a package unpack, compiler temporaries, an editor's safe write, `git gc`, log rotation with compression — is one shape (the deletions): no copy under an appended extension beside the deleted original, or copies that are plain, compressed or another known format. A user's own script encrypting 20 files a minute into copies with no known format header and deleting the originals (`openssl enc`, `ccrypt`) is recorded.

**How to test.** `ransom-check.sh` MS-23: the benign simulator (`ransom-sim.py`, /srv/nn-malsim only), in place and copy-delete, draws the Critical record (its kill held: the simulator finishes) and the posture reaches ENGAGED; tar, rsync, git checkout, an apt install and the simulator's own script compressing or moving its files then deleting them draw no record.

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/impact.rs::imp001_kills_the_actors_tree_on_two_shapes`, `agent/src/impact/host_tests.rs::copy_delete_beside_fresh_originals_is_decisive`, `agent/src/impact/host_tests.rs::benign_copy_delete_shapes_are_not_decisive`, `deploy/lab/malsim/ransom-check.sh::MS-23`

**ATT&CK note.** Data Encrypted for Impact (T1486) by the shape of the writes, not by a ransom note or a known family.

### NN-L-IMP-002_RenameExtensionBurst

Burst of renames to a new extension — category `impact_ransomware`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | High |
| Response | Log |
| ATT&CK | T1486 Data Encrypted for Impact (Impact) |
| Sensor — data | file (file_open LSM, FIM drift) — DC0061 File Modification |
| Validation | unit |

**Observes.** A burst of renames to one new extension, of an encryptor's shape, by one actor, alone (with a second shape it is NN-L-IMP-001).

**Known false positives.** Bulk renames by trusted writers (by identity and lineage); a user's own batch rename of many files to one extension is recorded.

**How to test.** From ONE process — the counter is per process, and a shell loop of `mv` is one process per file — rename 20 regular files of 4 KiB or more to `.locked`, with the LSM file-open sensor armed and no other shape: `python3 -c 'import glob,os; [os.rename(f, f + ".locked") for f in glob.glob("/srv/nn-test/*")]'`.

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/impact.rs::imp002_records_a_lone_rename_burst`

### NN-L-NET-001_OutboundToBlockedIp

Outbound to operator-blocked IP/CIDR — category `net_critical`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | Critical |
| Response | KillProcessTree |
| ATT&CK | T1071 Application Layer Protocol (Command and Control); T1095 Non-Application Layer Protocol (Command and Control) |
| Sensor — data | network (TCP connect, DNS, flows, listeners) — DC0082 Network Connection Creation, DC0078 Network Traffic Flow |
| Validation | unit (V2 Critical sub-gate) |

**Observes.** An outbound flow — at its connect, while it is open, at its close, or a connect refused by `--net-connect-deny` — whose destination address is in the operator's netflow blocklist (`/etc/northnarrow/netflow-blocklist.{v1,local}`, addresses and CIDRs). Never held back by the netflow rate limiter.

**Known false positives.** Only as good as the blocklist: an entry that covers a shared address (a CDN, a cloud load balancer) kills every client of it. The shipped list is empty.

**How to test.** Add an address the guest can reach (the lab host's bridge address) to `netflow-blocklist.local`, restart the agent, then connect to it from a throwaway shell: `sh -c 'curl -s --max-time 3 http://<address>/'`. The shell's tree is killed.

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/net.rs::net_001_fires_on_blocklist_match`

**ATT&CK note.** An indicator match: the destination, not the protocol, is the signal. Mapped to the two C2 channel techniques a flow to a known C2 address is an instance of (an application protocol, T1071, or raw TCP/UDP, T1095); the flow's protocol is not inspected.

### NN-L-NET-002_OutboundToBlockedTld

Outbound to operator-blocked TLD — category `net_high`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | High |
| Response | KillProcess |
| ATT&CK | T1090.003 Proxy: Multi-hop Proxy (Command and Control) |
| Sensor — data | network (TCP connect, DNS, flows, listeners) — DC0082 Network Connection Creation, DC0085 Network Traffic Content |
| Validation | unit |

**Observes.** An outbound flow whose process last looked up (within 5 minutes, same process) a name under `.onion` or `.bit`: the DNS cache names the flow's destination from the process's own query.

**Known false positives.** A Tor or Namecoin user on the host. A flow to an IP literal, or one whose name lookup the DNS sensor did not see, cannot fire it.

**How to test.** From one process, look up a `.onion` name (the resolver's NXDOMAIN is enough: the sensor records the query), then connect anywhere within 5 minutes: `python3 -c $'import socket, contextlib\nwith contextlib.suppress(OSError): socket.getaddrinfo("nn-test.onion", 80)\nsocket.create_connection(("<peer>", 80))'` (bash). The process is killed.

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/net.rs::net_002_fires_on_onion_tld`, `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/net.rs::net_002_no_hostname_no_fire`

**ATT&CK note.** `.onion` is Tor, T1090.003 Multi-hop Proxy. `.bit` (Namecoin) names have no ATT&CK technique of their own and are not mapped separately.

### NN-L-NET-003_BadJa3

JA3 fingerprint matches threat-actor blocklist — category `net_critical`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | Critical |
| Response | KillProcessTree |
| ATT&CK | T1573.002 Encrypted Channel: Asymmetric Cryptography (Command and Control) |
| Sensor — data | network (TCP connect, DNS, flows, listeners) — DC0085 Network Traffic Content |
| Validation | unit |

**Observes.** An outbound flow whose TLS ClientHello fingerprint (JA3) is in the operator's JA3 blocklist (`netflow-ja3-blocklist.{v1,local}`).

**Known false positives.** A JA3 hash names a TLS library and its settings, not a program: an entry shared by a common client (a language runtime's default TLS stack) kills every program built on it.

**How to test.** Cannot be exercised on a guest: no sensor fills a flow's TLS fingerprint until BUG-025 (`FlowTracker::attach_tls` has no caller), so the rule cannot fire. The unit test gives the flow a fingerprint directly.

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/net.rs::net_003_fires_on_ja3_blocklist_match`

**ATT&CK note.** TLS C2 is T1573.002 (ATT&CK classes SSL/TLS as asymmetric cryptography). Inactive until BUG-025: out of the V2 Critical sub-gate, still in its denominator.

### NN-L-NET-004_SuspiciousDnsQname

Unusually long DNS qname (recorded) — category `net_high`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | High, Medium |
| Response | Log |
| ATT&CK | T1071.004 Application Layer Protocol: DNS (Command and Control) |
| Sensor — data | network (TCP connect, DNS, flows, listeners) — DC0085 Network Traffic Content |
| Validation | unit+lab |

**Observes.** A DNS query for a name over 60 characters (Medium), or one whose name does not end in the kernel's linear copy of the datagram — sent in pieces, with UDP GSO or zero copy, or not DNS at all (High). Recorded, never killed; a forwarded leg is attributed to the process that asked the local stub.

**Known false positives.** Long legitimate names (object-storage buckets, CDN and load-balancer names, Kubernetes service FQDNs, ACME challenges) are recorded: external audit NETR-002 took the kill away for that reason. The local resolvers are never the target (FP-3), and one lookup's legs give one record (FP-5, shared with NN-L-NET-014).

**How to test.** Look up a name over 60 characters whose first label is under 25: `dig aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa.bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb.cccccccccccccccccccc.example.com`. `deploy/lab/dns-sensor/dns-sensor-check.sh` does it, and the name sent in pieces, with its own sender.

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/net.rs::net_004_records_a_long_qname`, `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/net.rs::net_004_logs_a_partial_name`, `deploy/lab/dns-sensor/dns-sensor-check.sh::NN-L-NET-004_SuspiciousDnsQname`

**ATT&CK note.** Length alone is the shape of a DNS tunnel (T1071.004), not proof of one; the encoded label is NN-L-NET-014's.

### NN-L-NET-005_DnsTxtNullBurst

DNS TXT/NULL burst (tunnelling shape) — category `net_high`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | High |
| Response | Log |
| ATT&CK | T1071.004 Application Layer Protocol: DNS (Command and Control) |
| Sensor — data | network (TCP connect, DNS, flows, listeners) — DC0085 Network Traffic Content |
| Validation | unit |

**Observes.** More than 50 DNS queries of type TXT or NULL from one process within 60 seconds, the record types DNS tunnels carry their payload in. Forwarded legs of the local resolvers are not counted.

**Known false positives.** Mail and anti-spam software checking SPF, DKIM and DMARC records in bulk, and service discovery over TXT. A burst asked through Varlink/nss-resolve (no stub query of the originator) is not counted at all (documented gap).

**How to test.** Send 60 TXT lookups from one process: `for i in $(seq 60); do echo "nn$i.example.com TXT"; done > /tmp/q; dig -f /tmp/q +short +tries=1 +time=1`.

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/net.rs::net_005_fires_on_txt_burst_over_threshold`, `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/net.rs::fp3_005_skips_forwarded_leg_but_fires_on_originator`

### NN-L-NET-006_UncommonListener

New listener on uncommon port — category `net_medium`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | Medium |
| Response | Log |
| ATT&CK | T1571 Non-Standard Port (Command and Control) |
| Sensor — data | network (TCP connect, DNS, flows, listeners) — DC0021 OS API Execution |
| Validation | unit+e2e |

**Observes.** A new TCP listener on a port outside 22, 53, 80, 443, 8080 and 8443 — or on one of them from a program not installed in a root-owned system tree — by a process outside the netflow comm allowlist. A wildcard bind is NN-L-NET-019's.

**Known false positives.** Developer servers, test fixtures and user services that listen on high ports; the netflow comm allowlist (judged on the executed program, not on `comm`) answers the known daemons.

**How to test.** Listen on loopback on an uncommon port from `python3`: `python3 -m http.server 18080 --bind 127.0.0.1`.

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/net.rs::net_006_fires_on_uncommon_port_non_allowlist_comm`, `agent/tests/net_privileged_e2e.rs::net_listener_on_uncommon_port_records_event`

**ATT&CK note.** A bind shell or a backdoor listener has no ATT&CK technique of its own; mapped to T1571 as the code names it. The protocol served on the port is not seen.

### NN-L-NET-007_Rfc1918FromUnusualProc

Outbound to RFC1918 from non-allowlist process — category `net_medium`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | Medium |
| Response | Log |
| ATT&CK | T1021 Remote Services (Lateral Movement); T1046 Network Service Discovery (Discovery) |
| Sensor — data | network (TCP connect, DNS, flows, listeners) — DC0082 Network Connection Creation, DC0078 Network Traffic Flow |
| Validation | unit |

**Observes.** An outbound flow to an internal address (RFC 1918, IPv6 unique-local or link-local) from a process outside the netflow comm allowlist, on any port.

**Known false positives.** Any internal client the allowlist does not name: monitoring agents, a developer's tools reaching a staging host, internal package mirrors. The four lateral-movement ports are NN-L-NET-018's.

**How to test.** From `python3`, connect to a port an RFC 1918 host on the lab network serves (not 445, 3389, 5985 or 5900): `python3 -c 'import socket; socket.create_connection(("<internal peer>", 8000), timeout=3)'`.

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/net.rs::net_007_fires_on_rfc1918_non_allowlist`, `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/net.rs::net_007_fires_on_link_local`

**ATT&CK note.** Evidence of internal reach, not of a protocol: a remote service (T1021) or a scan of internal services (T1046) draw it alike; the rule sees one flow at a time and does not tell them apart.

### NN-L-NET-008_OutboundFromTmpExec

Outbound from a staging-directory exec to non-resolver — category `net_high`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | High |
| Response | KillProcess, Log |
| ATT&CK | T1105 Ingress Tool Transfer (Command and Control) |
| Sensor — data | network (TCP connect, DNS, flows, listeners); exec (sched_process_exec, bprm_check_security) — DC0082 Network Connection Creation, DC0078 Network Traffic Flow, DC0034 Process Metadata |
| Validation | unit |

**Observes.** An outbound flow (at its connect, while it is open, at its close) from a process whose image lies in `/tmp`, `/var/tmp` or `/dev/shm` (named from the spawn cache or `/proc`), other than one to port 53 of a configured resolver. A process of a root package transaction is recorded (Log), not killed. To port 53 of a server that is no configured resolver — a match new in lab PR 224, which exempts only the host's resolvers — the kill is held behind the per-rule response policy (off by default): recorded at the same severity.

**Known false positives.** Installers and self-extracting archives that run a helper from a staging directory and call out; package-manager transactions are carved out. A staged exec followed by egress within 5 minutes is NN-L-CHAIN-002/005's (they run first).

**How to test.** In detect-only (R001 would kill the exec first), run a copy of `python3` from `/tmp` that connects more than 5 minutes after its exec, when the chain precursor is gone: `cp /usr/bin/python3 /tmp/nn-py; /tmp/nn-py -c 'import socket,time; time.sleep(330); socket.create_connection(("<peer>", 80))'`.

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/net.rs::net_008_fires_on_tmp_exec_outbound`, `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/net.rs::net_008_covers_every_staging_directory`, `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/net.rs::net_008_spares_a_package_transaction`

**ATT&CK note.** A staged payload calling out is mapped to its likeliest purpose, fetching the next stage (T1105); the flow's protocol is not seen, and a staged payload's C2 channel draws the rule as well.

### NN-L-NET-009_ByteAnomaly

Flow byte-count anomaly (possible exfiltration) — category `net_high`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | High |
| Response | Log |
| ATT&CK | T1048 Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol (Exfiltration); T1041 Exfiltration Over C2 Channel (Exfiltration) |
| Sensor — data | network (TCP connect, DNS, flows, listeners) — DC0078 Network Traffic Flow |
| Validation | unit |

**Observes.** A flow that sent more than 100 MiB, or UDP rows to one destination summing past 100 MiB within 10 minutes, from a process outside the netflow comm allowlist.

**Known false positives.** Backups, uploads, container image pushes and file sync by programs the allowlist does not name (`rsync`, `scp`, `git`, `curl` and the container runtimes are in it).

**How to test.** Send 120 MiB from `python3` to a listener on the lab host (`nc -l 9000 > /dev/null` there): `python3 -c 'import socket; s = socket.create_connection(("<peer>", 9000)); s.sendall(bytes(120 << 20))'`.

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/net.rs::net_009_fires_on_large_flow_from_non_allowlist`, `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/net.rs::net_009_sums_udp_rows_per_destination`

**ATT&CK note.** Volume only: whether the channel is the C2 channel (T1041) or another protocol (T1048) is not seen, so both are named.

### NN-L-NET-010_OutboundToHighRiskC2Port

Outbound to high-risk C2 port — category `net_high`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | High |
| Response | KillProcess, Log |
| ATT&CK | T1571 Non-Standard Port (Command and Control); T1090 Proxy (Command and Control) |
| Sensor — data | network (TCP connect, DNS, flows, listeners) — DC0082 Network Connection Creation, DC0078 Network Traffic Flow |
| Validation | unit+e2e |

**Observes.** An outbound flow to port 4444 (Metasploit's default), 1080 (SOCKS), 6667 or 6697 (IRC) or 9001 (Tor relays) from a process outside the netflow comm allowlist. A process named like an allowlisted program whose executable could not be read is recorded (Log), not killed. An allowlisted transfer tool (curl, wget, ssh, scp, sftp, rsync, git) whose lineage holds a precursor is judged as any program (lab PR 224); it was exempt before, so its kill is held behind the per-rule response policy (off by default).

**Known false positives.** IRC clients, SOCKS proxies and Tor run by a user, and services that happen to use these ports; 443 is deliberately not in the set (the rule kills).

**How to test.** With a listener on port 4444 of the lab host, connect from `python3`: `python3 -c 'import socket; socket.create_connection(("<peer>", 4444), timeout=3)'`. The process is killed.

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/net.rs::net_010_fires_on_c2_port_non_allowlist`, `agent/tests/detection_rules_at_scale_privileged_e2e.rs::net_outbound_high_risk_c2_port_trips_net_010`

**ATT&CK note.** 4444 and 6667/6697 are C2 on a non-standard port (T1571); 1080 SOCKS and 9001 Tor are proxies (T1090; 9001 is the multi-hop T1090.003).

### NN-L-NET-011_PlaintextCredService

Plaintext-credential service flow (FTP/Telnet) — category `net_medium`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | Medium |
| Response | Log |
| ATT&CK | T1071.002 Application Layer Protocol: File Transfer Protocols (Command and Control); T1021 Remote Services (Lateral Movement) |
| Sensor — data | network (TCP connect, DNS, flows, listeners) — DC0082 Network Connection Creation, DC0078 Network Traffic Flow |
| Validation | unit |

**Observes.** An outbound flow to FTP (21) or Telnet (23) from a process outside the netflow comm allowlist: credentials sent in clear.

**Known false positives.** Legacy FTP transfers and Telnet sessions to network equipment in environments that still use them; hence Log, not a kill.

**How to test.** With a listener on port 21 of the lab host, connect from `python3`: `python3 -c 'import socket; socket.create_connection(("<peer>", 21), timeout=3)'`.

### NN-L-NET-013_Beacon

Periodic outbound beacon (low jitter) — category `net_high`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | High |
| Response | Log |
| ATT&CK | T1071 Application Layer Protocol (Command and Control); T1029 Scheduled Transfer (Exfiltration) |
| Sensor — data | network (TCP connect, DNS, flows, listeners) — DC0078 Network Traffic Flow, DC0082 Network Connection Creation |
| Validation | unit |

**Observes.** Outbound flows from one process to one destination at regular intervals: at least 4 of them, a mean interval of a second or more and a coefficient of variation of 0.15 or less, within an hour.

**Known false positives.** Pollers, health checks, metrics exporters and update checkers not in the netflow comm allowlist (`chronyd`, `ntpd`, `node_exporter` are).

**How to test.** From one process, connect to the same address every 5 seconds: `python3 -c 'import socket, time; [(socket.create_connection(("<peer>", 80)).close(), time.sleep(5)) for _ in range(6)]'`.

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/net.rs::net_013_fires_on_low_jitter_periodic_flow`

**ATT&CK note.** The timing is the signal: a C2 beacon over an application protocol (T1071) or a scheduled transfer (T1029).

### NN-L-NET-014_DnsTunnelEntropy

DNS qname high-entropy label (tunnelling) — category `net_high`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | High, Medium |
| Response | KillProcess, Log |
| ATT&CK | T1071.004 Application Layer Protocol: DNS (Command and Control) |
| Sensor — data | network (TCP connect, DNS, flows, listeners) — DC0085 Network Traffic Content |
| Validation | unit |

**Observes.** A DNS query whose first label is 25 characters or more with a Shannon entropy of 3.8 bits per character or more. One such label is recorded (Medium); 8 distinct ones under one parent domain from one process within a minute kill it (High). A forwarded leg with no attributable originator is recorded only.

**Known false positives.** A long varied name of words (`my-company-prod-backups-archive`) reaches the threshold and is recorded; the kill needs a tunnel's volume of distinct labels (NETR-002). The local resolvers are never the target (FP-3).

**How to test.** Look up 8 random base32 labels under one parent from one process: `for i in $(seq 8); do echo "$(head -c 20 /dev/urandom | base32 | tr -d = | tr A-Z a-z).nn-tunnel.example.com"; done > /tmp/q; dig -f /tmp/q +short`. `dig` is killed; one label alone is recorded.

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/net.rs::net_014_kills_a_tunnel_of_distinct_labels_under_one_parent`, `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/net.rs::net_014_records_a_single_high_entropy_label`

**ATT&CK note.** DNS tunnelling carries C2 or exfiltrated data alike; the rule cannot tell them apart and is mapped to the DNS channel (T1071.004) only.

### NN-L-NET-018_Rfc1918LateralPort

RFC1918 outbound on lateral-movement port — category `net_high`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | High |
| Response | KillProcess, Log |
| ATT&CK | T1021.002 Remote Services: SMB/Windows Admin Shares (Lateral Movement); T1021.001 Remote Services: Remote Desktop Protocol (Lateral Movement); T1021.006 Remote Services: Windows Remote Management (Lateral Movement); T1021.005 Remote Services: VNC (Lateral Movement) |
| Sensor — data | network (TCP connect, DNS, flows, listeners) — DC0082 Network Connection Creation, DC0078 Network Traffic Flow |
| Validation | unit |

**Observes.** An outbound flow to an internal address (RFC 1918, IPv6 unique-local or link-local) on 445 (SMB), 3389 (RDP), 5985 (WinRM) or 5900 (VNC) from a process outside the netflow comm allowlist. A process named like an allowlisted program whose executable could not be read is recorded (Log). An allowlisted transfer tool whose lineage holds a precursor is judged as any program (lab PR 224), its kill held behind the per-rule response policy (off by default).

**Known false positives.** Administration clients (`smbclient`, RDP and VNC viewers) and monitoring of Windows hosts from this one, when not in the allowlist. SSH (22) is not watched (V2 row TQ04, a known gap).

**How to test.** With a listener on port 445 of an RFC 1918 lab host, connect from `python3`: `python3 -c 'import socket; socket.create_connection(("<internal peer>", 445), timeout=3)'`. The process is killed.

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/net.rs::net_018_fires_on_rfc1918_lateral_port_non_allowlist`, `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/net.rs::net_018_fires_on_ula_lateral_port`

**ATT&CK note.** One sub-technique per watched port; the port, not the protocol spoken on it, is what the rule sees.

### NN-L-NET-019_WildcardListener

Wildcard-bind listener on uncommon port — category `net_medium`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | Medium |
| Response | Log |
| ATT&CK | T1571 Non-Standard Port (Command and Control) |
| Sensor — data | network (TCP connect, DNS, flows, listeners) — DC0021 OS API Execution |
| Validation | unit+e2e |

**Observes.** A new TCP listener bound to the wildcard address (`0.0.0.0` or `::`) on an uncommon port — or on a common one from a program not installed in a root-owned system tree — by a process outside the netflow comm allowlist: the port is reachable from other hosts.

**Known false positives.** Developer servers and user services that bind all addresses by default (`python3 -m http.server`, test fixtures); the allowlist answers the known daemons.

**How to test.** Listen on all addresses on an uncommon port: `python3 -m http.server 18080`.

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/net.rs::net_019_fires_on_wildcard_uncommon_port_non_allowlist`, `agent/tests/detection_rules_at_scale_privileged_e2e.rs::net_wildcard_listener_trips_net_019`

**ATT&CK note.** As NN-L-NET-006: a backdoor listener has no technique of its own; T1571 as the code names it.

### NN-L-NET-020_DnsQueryFlood

DNS queries beyond the kernel's DNS budget — category `net_high`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | High |
| Response | Log |
| ATT&CK | T1071.004 Application Layer Protocol: DNS (Command and Control) |
| Sensor — data | network (TCP connect, DNS, flows, listeners) — DC0078 Network Traffic Flow |
| Validation | unit |

**Observes.** A process, or a user across its processes, sent at least 256 DNS queries beyond the kernel's DNS budget within 10 seconds (64, then 128 per second, per process; 2,048, then 1,024 per second, per user). Queries over the budget are not recorded, so the DNS rules never judge them.

**Known false positives.** DNS benchmarking and bulk resolution (crawlers, mail servers); the local resolvers' users are exempt in the kernel.

**How to test.** Send 3,000 queries from one process as fast as it can: `python3 -c 'import socket; s = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM); q = bytes.fromhex("123401000001000000000000076578616d706c6503636f6d0000010001"); [s.sendto(q, ("127.0.0.53", 53)) for _ in range(3000)]'` (a query for `example.com`).

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/net.rs::net_020_sums_held_queries_per_process_and_window`, `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/net.rs::net_020_user_budget_is_summed_per_user`

**ATT&CK note.** The queries held back were not judged: the rule reports the volume a DNS tunnel (T1071.004) could hide in, not their content.

### NN-L-NET-021_SensorRecordFlood

listen() or io_uring_setup() calls beyond the kernel's record budget — category `net_high`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | High |
| Response | Log |
| ATT&CK | T1685 Disable or Modify Tools (Defense Impairment) |
| Sensor — data | network (TCP connect, DNS, flows, listeners); io_uring (ring setup and use) — DC0021 OS API Execution |
| Validation | unit |

**Observes.** A process, or a user across its processes, made at least 256 `listen()` or `io_uring_setup()` calls beyond the kernel's record budget for that sensor within 10 seconds (64, then 128 per second, per process; 512, then 256 per second, per user): a flood that can push other processes' records out of the shared kernel ring.

**Known false positives.** Test suites and servers that create and close many listening sockets or rings in a tight loop.

**How to test.** Open and close 2,000 listeners from one process: `python3 -c 'import socket; [socket.create_server(("127.0.0.1", 0)).close() for _ in range(2000)]'`. The listeners recorded within the budget also draw NN-L-NET-006.

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/net.rs::net_021_names_the_listen_flooder_once_per_window`, `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/net.rs::net_021_sums_per_sensor_and_user`

**ATT&CK note.** The code named T1562.006 Indicator Blocking, revoked in v19, until lab PR 221; its replacement T1685 Disable or Modify Tools (Defense Impairment) covers blocking the telemetry a sensor collects.

### NN-L-NET-026_ScanFanOut

Outbound connects to many hosts or ports (scan fan-out) — category `net_high`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | High |
| Response | Log |
| ATT&CK | T1046 Network Service Discovery (Discovery) |
| Sensor — data | network (TCP connect, DNS, flows, listeners) — DC0082 Network Connection Creation |
| Validation | unit+lab |

**Observes.** Connect attempts and UDP sends of one process, or of the direct children of one parent, in a sliding window: 64 distinct hosts or 256 (host, port) pairs within 60 s is recorded; 512 hosts from one process is a second record, whose kill (`KillProcess`) is held behind the per-rule response policy, off by default (`--net-scan-*`).

**Known false positives.** Monitoring and orchestration (Prometheus, Zabbix, Nagios, kubelet, Ansible, … and `--net-fanout-exempt`) are exempt by lineage: the name of the executable the kernel ran, in a root-owned system tree, never the comm a process sets; a raised threshold (flag or environment) is a signed weakening.

**How to test.** `net-check.sh --only MS21`: a sweep of a loopback /24 from one process, a port scan of one host.

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/net_fanout.rs::a_sweep_is_recorded_then_killed_at_the_kill_threshold`, `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/net_fanout.rs::a_port_scan_of_one_host_is_recorded_on_the_pairs`, `deploy/lab/malsim/net-check.sh::MS21`

### NN-L-NET-027_OutboundAuthBruteforce

Repeated outbound connects to authentication services (brute force) — category `net_high`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | High |
| Response | Log |
| ATT&CK | T1110 Brute Force (Credential Access) |
| Sensor — data | network (TCP connect, DNS, flows, listeners) — DC0082 Network Connection Creation |
| Validation | unit+lab |

**Observes.** Connects of one process (or of one parent's children) to authentication services — SSH, Telnet, RDP, VNC ports — in a sliding window: 20 within 300 s is recorded; 100 from one process is a second record, whose kill (`KillProcess`) is held behind the per-rule response policy, off by default (`--net-brute-*`).

**Known false positives.** Configuration management that opens many SSH sessions (Ansible and the other exempt programs, by lineage); a jump host's own users.

**How to test.** `net-check.sh --only MS21`: repeated connects to a loopback SSH port.

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/net_fanout.rs::repeated_ssh_connects_are_a_brute_force`, `deploy/lab/malsim/net-check.sh::MS21`

**ATT&CK note.** Outbound only: the connects are counted, not the credentials tried.

### NN-L-CANARY-001_FileAccess

Canary file access — category `canary_deception`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | Critical, High, Low |
| Response | KillProcessTree, Log |
| ATT&CK | T1005 Data from Local System (Collection) |
| Sensor — data | canary trip; file (file_open LSM, FIM drift); exec (sched_process_exec, bprm_check_security) — DC0055 File Access, DC0032 Process Creation |
| Validation | e2e-event (V2 Critical sub-gate) |

**Observes.** An open (or an exec) of a File canary, a decoy file the operator deployed with `nn-admin canary deploy file`, matched by inode against the signed canary registry before the rule engine runs.

**Known false positives.** No workflow reads a decoy, but a program that reads whole trees (backup, anti-malware, indexer, sync: the built-in canary readers and the signed canary-readers.local) is recorded High, not killed (external audit DEC-005); every access after the first trip is a Low record (DEC-004).

**How to test.** Deploy a File canary (`nn-admin canary deploy --name t --key <key> file --path /root/aws_keys_old.txt`) and `cat` it from a shell: the shell's tree is killed, the posture goes to COMBAT.

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/canary.rs::canary001_fires_on_file_canary_file_open`, `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/canary.rs::a_reader_of_whole_trees_is_recorded_not_killed`, `agent/tests/canary_privileged_e2e.rs::file_canary_open_triggers_canary_tripped_event_and_combat`

**ATT&CK note.** The technique is what the intruder did: read a file found on the host (T1005). A decoy named for credentials is NN-L-CANARY-004's (T1552.001).

### NN-L-CANARY-002_ProcessExec

Canary process executed — category `canary_deception`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | Critical, Low |
| Response | KillProcessTree, Log |
| ATT&CK | T1083 File and Directory Discovery (Discovery) |
| Sensor — data | canary trip; exec (sched_process_exec, bprm_check_security) — DC0032 Process Creation |
| Validation | e2e-event (V2 Critical sub-gate) |

**Observes.** An exec of a Process canary, a decoy helper binary the operator deployed with `nn-admin canary deploy process`, matched by path against the signed canary registry.

**Known false positives.** No workflow runs the decoy (operators use nn-admin); an exec after the first trip is a Low record (DEC-004).

**How to test.** Deploy a Process canary (`nn-admin canary deploy --name t --key <key> process --path /usr/local/bin/sysadmin-helper --fake-arg0 helper`) and run it: the caller's tree is killed.

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/canary.rs::canary002_fires_on_process_canary_exec`, `agent/tests/canary_privileged_e2e.rs::process_canary_exec_triggers_canary_tripped_event_and_combat`

**ATT&CK note.** Weak mapping: no ATT&CK technique names running a decoy. The decoy is found by enumerating a binary directory (T1083, design appendix B: `ls /usr/local/bin` then exec something interesting); the exec itself is what the rule sees.

### NN-L-CANARY-003_NetworkConnect

Canary network connect — category `canary_deception`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | Critical |
| Response | KillProcessTree |
| ATT&CK | T1046 Network Service Discovery (Discovery); T1021 Remote Services (Lateral Movement) |
| Sensor — data | canary trip; network (TCP connect, DNS, flows, listeners) — DC0082 Network Connection Creation |
| Validation | e2e (V2 Critical sub-gate) |

**Observes.** A TCP connect by a local process (the connect kprobe) to a Network canary's address and port, a destination no legitimate process uses.

**Known false positives.** The operator's own scanner or monitoring check that probes the canary's port trips it; a deploy is refused when a listener on the host would receive the canary's connections. Every connect kills; a connection from another host is not seen.

**How to test.** Deploy a Network canary (`nn-admin canary deploy --name t --key <key> network --bind-addr 127.0.0.1 --bind-port 4444`) and connect to it from a shell (`bash -c 'exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/4444'`).

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/canary.rs::canary003_fires_on_network_canary_connect`, `agent/src/canary/detector_tests.rs::a_network_canary_trip_draws_canary_003_on_the_connector`, `agent/tests/canary_privileged_e2e.rs::network_canary_connect_trips_canary_003_and_kills_the_connector`

**ATT&CK note.** A port scan of the host finds the decoy (T1046); a decoy destination planted in a configuration file, a hosts entry or an ssh config is a remote service the intruder tries to reach (T1021).

### NN-L-CANARY-004_CredentialRead

Canary credential read — category `canary_deception`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | Critical, High, Low |
| Response | KillProcessTree, Log |
| ATT&CK | T1552.001 Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files (Credential Access) |
| Sensor — data | canary trip; file (file_open LSM, FIM drift); exec (sched_process_exec, bprm_check_security) — DC0055 File Access, DC0032 Process Creation |
| Validation | unit (V2 Critical sub-gate) |

**Observes.** A read of a Credential canary, a decoy credential file (aws, azure, gcp, docker or generic family, format-valid and authenticating nowhere) the operator deployed with `nn-admin canary deploy credential`.

**Known false positives.** Legitimate cloud CLIs read the real credentials, not the decoy; a reader of whole trees is recorded High, not killed (DEC-005), and an access after the first trip is a Low record (DEC-004).

**How to test.** Deploy a Credential canary (`nn-admin canary deploy --name t --key <key> credential --path /root/.aws/credentials.bak --cred-family aws`) and `grep -r AKIA /root` from a shell.

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/canary.rs::canary004_fires_on_credential_canary_read`, `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/canary.rs::a_later_access_to_a_tripped_canary_is_recorded_not_killed`

### NN-L-CHAIN-001_CredReadThenEgress

Credential-store access followed by network egress — category `chain_exfiltration`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | Critical, High |
| Response | KillProcessTree, Log |
| ATT&CK | T1555.003 Credentials from Password Stores: Credentials from Web Browsers (Credential Access); T1555.005 Credentials from Password Stores: Password Managers (Credential Access); T1552.004 Unsecured Credentials: Private Keys (Credential Access); T1041 Exfiltration Over C2 Channel (Exfiltration) |
| Sensor — data | network (TCP connect, DNS, flows, listeners); file (file_open LSM, FIM drift) — DC0078 Network Traffic Flow, DC0055 File Access |
| Validation | unit (V2 Critical sub-gate) |

**Observes.** An outbound flow from a process that read a FIM-watched credential store (a browser's, a password manager's database, a GPG keyring) within 300 s: Critical kill; within 30 minutes, one High record (NETR-014).

**Known false positives.** A browser or password manager whose store the operator added to the FIM watch list, syncing within the window. Reads seen only through the open sensor's wide coverage of the homes are not a precursor (NETR-001).

**How to test.** With a browser credential file (`Login Data`) in the FIM watch list, one process reads it and connects out (loopback counts); run the agent in detect-only mode, since NN-L-FIM-015 acts on the read first.

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/chain.rs::chain001_fires_on_cred_read_then_egress`, `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/chain.rs::an_aged_read_is_recorded_once`

**ATT&CK note.** The credential stores of the precursor are those of NN-L-FIM-015, -016 and -017 (T1555.003, T1555.005, T1552.004); the egress is read as exfiltration over the process's own channel (T1041).

### NN-L-CHAIN-002_TmpExecThenEgress

/tmp exec followed by network egress — category `chain_c2`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | Critical |
| Response | KillProcessTree |
| ATT&CK | T1059 Command and Scripting Interpreter (Execution); T1571 Non-Standard Port (Command and Control) |
| Sensor — data | network (TCP connect, DNS, flows, listeners); exec (sched_process_exec, bprm_check_security) — DC0078 Network Traffic Flow, DC0032 Process Creation |
| Validation | e2e (V2 Critical sub-gate) |

**Observes.** An outbound flow (at its connect, while it is open, at its close), other than one to port 53 of a configured resolver, from a process whose image is in a staging directory (/tmp, /var/tmp, /dev/shm), within 300 s of its exec. To port 53 of a server that is no configured resolver — a match new in lab PR 224, which exempts only the host's resolvers — the kill is held behind the per-rule response policy (off by default): recorded at the same severity. It also completes when the exec record is processed after the flow (lab PR 244), judged on the kernel timestamps.

**Known false positives.** An installer or a test binary run from a temporary directory that talks to the network. A process of a package transaction is spared (NETR-008, lab PR 175); its flow falls to NN-L-NET-008.

**How to test.** Run from /tmp a helper that connects out as its first act (the e2e compiles one, which wins the race against R001's kill), or run the agent in detect-only mode and `cp /usr/bin/curl /tmp/c && /tmp/c http://127.0.0.1:8080/`.

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/chain.rs::chain002_fires_on_tmp_exec_then_nondns_egress`, `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/chain.rs::chain002_completes_when_the_exec_is_processed_after_the_egress`, `agent/tests/detection_rules_at_scale_privileged_e2e.rs::chain_tmp_exec_then_egress_trips_chain_002`

**ATT&CK note.** T1059 and T1571 as the design and the V2 technique rows (TQ18, TQ55) have them. The image need not be an interpreter, and the trigger is any port but 53, so a payload calling home on 443 (T1071) fires it too, which the mapping does not claim.

### NN-L-CHAIN-003_CanaryThenEgress

Canary trip followed by network egress — category `chain_exfiltration`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | Critical, High |
| Response | KillProcessTree, Log |
| ATT&CK | T1041 Exfiltration Over C2 Channel (Exfiltration) |
| Sensor — data | network (TCP connect, DNS, flows, listeners); canary trip — DC0078 Network Traffic Flow, DC0055 File Access, DC0032 Process Creation, DC0082 Network Connection Creation |
| Validation | unit (V2 Critical sub-gate) |

**Observes.** An outbound flow from a process that tripped a deception canary (any NN-L-CANARY type) within 300 s: Critical kill; within 30 minutes, one High record (NETR-014). The connection a network canary trip is (its connect, answered by NN-L-CANARY-003) is not an egress after it: no row of it completes the chain, in whatever order its connect and close arrive (lab PR 246).

**Known false positives.** Every trip is a precursor, including one the canary rule only records: a reader of whole trees (a backup client) that reads a canary and then uploads within 300 s draws the Critical verdict.

**How to test.** Deploy a File canary, then from one process read it and connect out (`python3 -c` opening the decoy, then a socket); run the agent in detect-only mode, since NN-L-CANARY-001 kills the reader first.

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/chain.rs::chain003_fires_on_canary_then_egress`, `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/chain.rs::chain003_records_an_aged_trip_without_killing`, `agent/src/canary/detector_tests.rs::the_trips_own_connection_draws_no_chain_verdict_in_any_order`

**ATT&CK note.** The precursor's technique depends on the canary type (see NN-L-CANARY-001..004); the chain itself is evidence of exfiltration.

### NN-L-IOU-001_IoUringRingCreated

io_uring ring created by an unlisted process — category `defense_evasion`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | Low |
| Response | Log |

| Sensor — data | io_uring (ring setup and use) — DC0021 OS API Execution |
| Validation | unit+lab |

**Observes.** The creation of an io_uring ring by a process outside the known io_uring users and the process allowlist, judged on the executable the kernel ran: the baseline of who uses io_uring on the host.

**Known false positives.** Any legitimate io_uring user not yet listed (a database, QEMU, nginx, a liburing tool, a libuv runtime such as Node 20 or later); add it to process-comm-allowlist.local.

**How to test.** anti-tamper.sh case C22 builds a probe that opens and reads /etc/hostname and connects to 127.0.0.1:9 through one ring (`kernel.io_uring_disabled` must be 0).

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/iouring.rs::ring_creation_logs_unlisted_and_exempts_known_and_allowlisted`, `deploy/lab/adversarial/anti-tamper.sh::case C22`

**ATT&CK note.** The reasoning text named T1562 (Impair Defenses), revoked in ATT&CK v19, until lab PR 221 (its successor T1685 is disabling or tampering with a tool, which a ring does not do). io_uring does I/O outside the syscalls the open, exec and connect sensors hook: calling a kernel interface directly to sidestep hooked APIs is T1106.
