### NN-L-AT-001_AntiTamperDenial

Attempt on the agent refused by an anti-tamper hook — category `anti_tamper`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | High |
| Response | Log |
| ATT&CK | T1685 Disable or Modify Tools (Defense Impairment); T1055.008 Process Injection: Ptrace System Calls (Stealth); T1055.009 Process Injection: Proc Memory (Stealth); T1552.004 Unsecured Credentials: Private Keys (Credential Access) |
| Sensor — data | anti-tamper (LSM denials, bpf() syscalls) — DC0035 Process Access, DC0061 File Modification, DC0040 File Deletion, DC0055 File Access, DC0021 OS API Execution |
| Validation | unit+lab |

**Observes.** Every action on the agent an anti-tamper LSM hook refused: a signal to a protected pid, a ptrace or /proc/&lt;pid&gt;/mem access, a write, unlink, rename or new entry in its protected files, a handle to its BPF maps or links, a kexec load, a read of its signing key. Issued by process_event outside the engine.

**Known false positives.** An administrator's `systemctl stop` or `kill` of the agent, or an upgrade, outside a trusted-installer window; a debugger or `strace -p` on the agent. The kernel refused the action either way; the record is Log only.

**How to test.** `kill -9` the agent from a root shell (anti-tamper.sh case C01) or read /proc/&lt;agent&gt;/mem (case C03): the record names the refused operation (deny=signal, deny=ptrace).

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/anti_tamper.rs::every_denial_kind_is_a_high_log_verdict`, `deploy/lab/adversarial/anti-tamper.sh::case C01`, `deploy/lab/adversarial/anti-tamper.sh::case C03`

**ATT&CK note.** Killing, stopping or rewriting the sensor is T1685. A ptrace or /proc/&lt;pid&gt;/mem access on the agent is the injection attempt the V2 rows TQ13 and TQ15 expect denied (T1055.008, T1055.009); a read of the signing key is T1552.004.

### NN-L-EPG-001_CredentialPostcondition

Credentials gained without a legitimate kernel transition — category `privilege_escalation`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | Critical, High |
| Response | KillProcess, Log |
| ATT&CK | T1068 Exploitation for Privilege Escalation (Privilege Escalation) |
| Sensor — data | exploit guard (commit_creds, namespace and root switches; capable, exec and file_open in lite, raw_syscalls in strict) — DC0034 Process Metadata, DC0021 OS API Execution |
| Validation | unit (V2 Critical sub-gate) |

**Observes.** A task that was not fully privileged holding a uid, a gid, a capability or another user namespace that no commit_creds made, or that commit_creds made on behalf of a system call that never makes that change: the post-condition of a kernel exploit, whatever its bug. Lite (default) judges the mechanism on the call in progress and a credential changed without one at its first use (capable, exec, a root-private open); strict compares around every system call. High, Log only: lite's degraded evidence, a task whose record the LRU task map evicted, re-taken holding uid or gid 0 or a capability that no mechanism is known to have given. Issued by process_event outside the engine.

**Known false positives.** None expected from the legitimate transitions (sudo, su, newgrp, setpriv, capsh, unshare, rootless and rootful containers, systemd-run --uid, cron): the guard allows by mechanism, not by name, and lite compares real_cred so overlayfs's override_creds is not a change. Experimental: detect by default; enforce kills in kernel (lite also refuses the use). The High degraded evidence fires for legitimate privileged tasks too when the lite task map evicts (a host above its size, or a task flood; counted and attested).

**How to test.** On a debug build, `epg-check.sh inject capable detect` (lite) or `inject getppid detect` (strict; the agent refuses strict below Linux 6.1): the injected anomaly is recorded, the record naming the probe (comm nn-epg-probe) and, in its response, the point that caught it (the journal's VERDICT line says LAB INJECTION); `negative` runs the legitimate transitions and expects no record.

**Tests.** `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/epg.rs::credential_write_in_detect_mode_is_a_critical_log`, `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/epg.rs::enforce_kill_is_recorded_as_a_kernel_kill`, `crates/nn-core/src/decision/rules/epg.rs::a_lost_baseline_is_degraded_evidence`, `deploy/lab/epg/epg-check.sh::inject`

**ATT&CK note.** Exploitation for Privilege Escalation (T1068) by its result: the rule sees the credentials an exploit leaves, not the exploit.

Namespaces or root left without a legitimate kernel transition — category `escape_to_host`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity | Critical |
| Response | KillProcess, Log |
| ATT&CK | T1611 Escape to Host (Privilege Escalation) |
| Sensor — data | exploit guard (commit_creds, namespace and root switches; capable, exec and file_open in lite, raw_syscalls in strict) — DC0034 Process Metadata, DC0021 OS API Execution |
| Validation | unit (V2 Critical sub-gate) |
